name: Brunissen

attributes.attribute: her name means the brown one or the brown queen
an orphan in the forest of Brocéliande
eased by the song of magical birds
connected by some with land-abundance deities

sources: Markale, Jean. Women of the Celts. Rochester, Vt.: Inner Traditions, 1986, 74-75, 111.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Brunissen is a fairy queen from Provence in France. Her name means the brown one. She is the brown queen. Her tale recalls Celtic bird goddesses such as Rhiannon. While orphaned in Brocéliande, she wept a full seven years. Magic birdsong alone soothed her. A Round Table knight named Giflet, or Jaufré, drew her from her grief. Some connect her with deities of the land's abundance.

okr.objective: Describe Brunissen, the fairy queen of Provence.
key_results: Brunissen was a fairy queen of Provence.
Her name means the brown one.
She wept for seven years as an orphan in Brocéliande.
The knight Giflet, or Jaufré, drew her from her grief.
